- **Azimuth:** 275.986° (which is roughly northwest)
- **Illumination:** 5.75% (a new moon phase, but not quite new — it's a waxing crescent)

---

- **Altitude:** -23.762° (also below the horizon)
- **Azimuth:** 281.646° (which is northwest, similar to the Moon)

This suggests that both the Sun and the Moon are below the horizon at this time, which is consistent with it being **nighttime** in Perth.

---

### 🌌 **Sky Conditions:**

- **Sky brightness:** Night (clear)
- **Visibility:** Clear sky
- **Observer:** Ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight

---

### ✅ **Can You Spot the Moon?**

**Short Answer:** **No.** You won't be able to see the Moon at this time.

**Longer Explanation:**

- The **Moon is 52 degrees below the horizon**, which is well below the visible horizon. Even with clear skies, the Moon is **not visible** at this time.

- The **Sun is also below the horizon**, so the sky is dark, and the Moon would be in a dark sky, making it even harder to see if it were above the horizon.

---

### 🕰️ **When Will the Moon Be Visible?**

Since the Moon is currently below the horizon, it will be visible again when it rises above the horizon. In Perth, the Moon typically rises around **10:00 PM to 11:00 PM** in July, depending on the exact date and phase.

You might want to check the **Moonrise time** for **2026-07-12** in Perth to know when it will be visible. You can use an astronomy app or a time and date website for precise times.

---

### ✅ **Summary:**

- **Moon is below the horizon** at 19:25 AWST on 2026-07-12.
- **Not visible** with the naked eye at this time.
- **Moonrise time** will be later in the evening — likely around 10:00–11:00 PM.

---

If you're looking for a **good time to see the Moon**, you might want to wait until it rises, and if the Moon is in a **waxing crescent phase**, you might be able to see a very thin sliver of it just after it rises, depending on the lighting conditions and your location.
